## Findings (most severe first)

1. **Low: `pnpm.overrides` does nothing under Bun** (`package.json`). The project installs with Bun, which reads top-level `overrides`/`resolutions`, not `pnpm.overrides`. Today it doesn't matter: `bun.lock` already resolves `entities` to 4.5.0 for `@react-email/render`, and `htmlparser2` keeps its own 7.0.1. If a later install drifts, move the pin to a top-level `"overrides"` block. No action needed now.
2. **Low: `sendNotificationEmail` accepts any `buttonUrl`** (`src/lib/email-templates/send-email.ts`). Nothing calls it yet. CC-3 should only pass links it builds itself from `https://mychata.cz` and never text typed by another user as the URL; heading and paragraph are escaped by React, so text is safe.
3. **Low, cosmetic: the auth preview route names the site "My Chata Hub" and uses the lovable.app URL as sample data** (`src/routes/lovable/email/auth/preview.ts`). Only Lovable's preview panel sees it; real mails use "MyChata" and `https://mychata.cz` (webhook.ts, layout.tsx).
4. **Info: invite, magic-link and reauthentication templates exist** although the app doesn't send them; Lovable says every type needs a template. They are styled and point at mychata.cz. Fine.
5. **Info: the Lovable "Emails" panel header shows "My Chata Hub <noreply@mychata.cz>" and an English subject**, while the code sends "MyChata <no-reply@notify.mychata.cz>" with "Potvrďte svůj e-mail · Confirm your email". Check the real From and subject in the next received mail (F-07 test).

Checked and fine: React-escaped text in all templates; Czech first with English under it; links built from `https://mychata.cz`; Reply-To `podpora@mychata.cz`; `LOVABLE_API_KEY` read server-side only; preview routes compare a bearer key, webhook verification is done by `@lovable.dev/email-js`; no personal data added (preview data uses `user@example.test` and an invented name).

Merge: yes (already merged; follow-ups 1–2 belong to CC-3).
